summary: Tested HYPEUSDT (Bitunix) integration, scanner_settings key-persistence fix, optimizer/apply, custom-strategy persistence and the new Strategie-Copilot (backend + UI). 18 pytest cases created in /app/backend/tests/test_iter27_copilot_hype_settings.py: 16 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The single failure is a real, reproducible blocker: POST /api/copilot/chat takes 200-280s (measured 3m20s and 4m36s locally) and therefore returns 502 Bad Gateway through the public ingress (~60s timeout) - the Copilot chat is unusable from the browser. All other Copilot endpoints (status/apply/review/history/DELETE history, auth guards, 400/422 error paths) work correctly. Frontend: page loads, HYPE appears as 11th entry in TOP 10 COINS and its chart loads with live Bitunix candles, Tools -> Strategie-Optimizer modal opens, strategy-copilot panel with toggle/quick-prompts/input/send works in both Optimizer and StrategyBuilder, thinking indicator shows - but the reply never arrives due to the 502.

critical.issue: Request duration 200-280s -> public ingress returns 502 Bad Gateway (HTML), frontend shows only 'Copilot denkt nach...' then a generic error toast. Reproduced via pytest (external URL, 502 after ~60s) and via UI (RESP 502 POST copilot/chat). Locally (localhost:8001) the same request completes with a valid German reply after 3m20s / 4m36s, so the logic is correct but far too slow. Root causes: (a) services/ai_providers.py line ~674 creates AsyncOpenAI(...) WITHOUT a timeout -> openai default 600s, so a slow OpenRouter free model can hang for minutes; (b) chosen free models (nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free, nemotron-3-ultra-550b) are extremely slow/queued and the same keys are concurrently used by the KI-Trader engine; (c) empty-response retry adds another full round trip (log: 'leere Antwort - einmaliger Retry in 2s'). Fix: per-request timeout (~30-45s) for the copilot chain + fail over to the next model, and/or make the chat asynchronous (job id + polling / SSE) so the HTTP request returns within the ingress limit.

minor.issue: The user message is persisted (copilot_chat) BEFORE the LLM call; when the call fails/times out the history keeps an orphan user message with no assistant reply.
404 - no read endpoint to verify the copilot_note memory bridge from outside; only verifiable in DB (test skipped).

integration_issues.issue: Send works, optimistic user bubble + 'Copilot denkt nach...' appear, but the fetch gets a 502 HTML response after ~60s; res.json() on the HTML body throws so the user only sees the generic catch-toast 'Verbindungsfehler zum Copilot' instead of a meaningful message. Suggest surfacing a timeout-specific hint once the backend latency is fixed.

issues: React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' - invalid HTML inside a <select> (harmless but should be cleaned up)

action_items: Add an explicit request timeout (30-45s) for the Copilot OpenRouter calls (AsyncOpenAI(timeout=...) in services/ai_providers.py) and/or turn /api/copilot/chat into an async job (POST returns id, GET polls) so it never exceeds the ~60s ingress limit
Prefer fast OpenRouter free models for the copilot chain and skip models that already timed out (short cooldown)
Only persist the user message after a successful LLM reply (or mark failed turns) to avoid orphan history entries
Show a specific error message in StrategyCopilot when the response is not JSON (502/timeout) instead of the generic 'Verbindungsfehler'
Optional: fix invalid <span> inside <option> markup (React hydration warning)

rca_of_the_issue: POST /api/copilot/chat -> StrategyCopilot.chat -> ai_providers.generate_chain -> _oai_generate uses a cached AsyncOpenAI client created without a timeout (default 600s). The OpenRouter free models in the chain (nvidia/nemotron-*:free) respond only after several minutes (plus a 2s empty-response retry), so the HTTP request outlives the Kubernetes/Cloudflare ingress timeout (~60s) and the browser/pytest receives a 502 Bad Gateway HTML page while the backend later logs 200 OK. Mitigation: bound the per-call time (timeout + next-model failover) or decouple the request from the LLM call via a polling/streaming endpoint.
